q: Relative density is how much a substance is denser than _____.
e: Relative density is how much a substance is denser than water. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies involving substance.

q: Relative density is also known as _____.
e: Relative density is also known as specific gravity. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies. Absolute density: mass per unit volume.

q: The formula for relative density is the density of substance divided by the density of water at _____.
e: The formula for relative density is the density of substance divided by the density of water at $4^{\circ}\text{C}$. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: As the density of water is $1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ in CGS units, the density of substance can be taken as the _____.
e: As the density of water is $1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ in CGS units, the density of substance can be taken as the relative density. Relative density here means mass per unit volume. Absolute density: mass per unit volume.

q: Relative density is just a number without _____.
e: Relative density is just a number without unit. Unit here means an agreed amount you use as the scale of a measurement.

q: Archimedes' Principle Part I states that an immersed object displaces liquid volume equal to the volume of the _____ portion.
e: Archimedes' Principle Part I states that an immersed object displaces liquid volume equal to the volume of the immersed portion. The physics in this sentence is built around immersed.

q: Archimedes' Principle Part II states that the loss in weight of the object is equal to the _____ of the liquid displaced.
e: Archimedes' Principle Part II states that the loss in weight of the object is equal to the weight of the liquid displaced. Weight here means the gravitational pull of the Earth on a body, a downward force. Mass: the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location.

q: The upward thrust acting on a body immersed in a liquid is equal to the weight of the _____ displaced by the body.
e: The upward thrust acting on a body immersed in a liquid is equal to the weight of the liquid displaced by the body. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: Upward thrust is also known as uplift force or _____.
e: Upward thrust is also known as uplift force or buoyancy. Buoyancy names upward thrust is also known as uplift force or.

q: By Archimedes' principle, if the weight of a body is more than buoyancy, it will _____ in the liquid.
e: By Archimedes' principle, if the weight of a body is more than buoyancy, it will sink in the liquid. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: Substances having relative density greater than _____ will sink in water.
e: Substances having relative density greater than one will sink in water. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies involving density.
